Securities and Exchange Commission
[Release No. 34-106640; File No. SR-CboeBZX-2026-084]
October 8, 2026.
Pursuant to Section 19(b)(1) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 (“Act”),
[
1
]
and Rule 19b-4 thereunder,
[
2
]
notice is hereby given that on October 1, 2026, Cboe BZX Exchange, Inc. (“Exchange” or “BZX”) filed with the
(
printed page 65273)
Securities and Exchange Commission (“Commission”) the proposed rule change as described in Items I, II, and III below, which Items have been prepared by the Exchange. The Commission is publishing this notice to solicit comments on the proposed rule change from interested persons.
I. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement of the Terms of Substance of the Proposed Rule Change
Cboe BZX Exchange, Inc. (the “Exchange” or “BZX”) proposes to amend its Fee Schedule by introducing Step-Up Tier 1 under footnote 2 of its Fee Schedule. The text of the proposed rule change is provided in Exhibit 5.
The text of the proposed rule change is also available on the Commission's website (
https://www.sec.gov/​rules/​sro.shtml
), the Exchange's website (
https://www.cboe.com/​us/​equities/​regulation/​rule_​filings/​bzx/​
), and at the principal office of the Exchange.
II. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement of the Purpose of, and Statutory Basis for, the Proposed Rule Change
In its filing with the Commission, the Exchange included statements concerning the purpose of and basis for the proposed rule change and discussed any comments it received on the proposed rule change. The text of these statements may be examined at the places specified in Item IV below. The Exchange has prepared summaries, set forth in sections A, B, and C below, of the most significant aspects of such statements.
A. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement of the Purpose of, and Statutory Basis for, the Proposed Rule Change
1. Purpose
The Exchange proposes to amend its Fee Schedule applicable to its equities trading platform (“BZX Equities”) by introducing Step-Up Tier 1 under footnote 2 of its Fee Schedule. The Exchange proposes to implement these changes effective on October 1, 2026.
The Exchange first notes that it operates in a highly competitive market in which market participants can readily direct order flow to competing venues if they deem fee levels at a particular venue to be excessive or incentives to be insufficient. More specifically, the Exchange is only one of 17 registered equities exchanges, as well as a number of alternative trading systems and other off-exchange venues that do not have similar self-regulatory responsibilities under the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 (the “Act”), to which market participants may direct their order flow. Based on publicly available information,
[
3
]
no single registered equities exchange has more than 15% of the market share. Thus, in such a low-concentrated and highly competitive market, no single equities exchange possesses significant pricing power in the execution of order flow.
The Exchange in particular operates a “Maker-Taker” model whereby it pays rebates to members that add liquidity and assesses fees to those that remove liquidity. The Exchange's Fee Schedule sets forth the standard rebates and rates applied per share for orders that provide and remove liquidity, respectively. Currently, for orders in securities priced at or above $1.00, the Exchange provides a standard rebate of $0.00160 per share for orders that add liquidity and assesses a fee of $0.0030 per share for orders that remove liquidity.
[
4
]
For orders in securities priced below $1.00, the Exchange does not provide a rebate for orders that add liquidity and assesses a fee of 0.30% of the total dollar value for orders that remove liquidity.
[
5
]
Additionally, in response to the competitive environment, the Exchange also offers tiered pricing which provides Members opportunities to qualify for higher rebates or reduced fees where certain volume criteria and thresholds are met. Tiered pricing provides an incremental incentive for Members to strive for higher tier levels, which provides increasingly higher benefits or discounts for satisfying increasingly more stringent criteria.
Step-Up Tiers
Footnote 2 of the Fee Schedule is currently designated as “Reserved.” The Exchange now proposes to designate footnote 2 of the Fee Schedule as “Step-Up Tiers,” where the Exchange would offer various Step-Up Tiers that provide enhanced rebates for orders yielding fee codes B,
[
6
]
V,
[
7
]
and Y
[
8
]
where a Member reaches certain add volume-based criteria, including “growing” its volume over a certain baseline month. The Exchange also proposes to introduce Step-Up Tier 1. The proposed criteria of proposed Step-Up Tier 1 is as follows:
Proposed Step-Up Tier 1 will provide a rebate of $0.0028 per share to qualifying orders where: (1) Member has a Step-Up Add TCV
[
9
]
from September 2026 ≥ 0.08% or Member has an Ex-Subdollar Step-Up Add Ex-Subdollar TCV
[
10
]
from September 2026 ≥ 0.08%; and (2) Member has a CMC ADV of 300,000 that yield fee code MC.
[
11
]
For purposes of the proposed Step-Up Tier 1, “CMC ADV” means ADV in Cboe Market Close (“CMC”) orders.
[
12
]
In addition, the Exchange proposes to add the definition of “Step-Up Add TCV”
[
13
]
and “Ex-Subdollar Step-Up Add Ex-Subdollar TCV”
[
14
]
to the Definitions section of the Fee Schedule. The Exchange also proposes to revise the Fee Codes and Associated Fees table on the Fee Schedule to include footnote 2 on fee codes B, V, and Y. The Exchange also notes that proposed Step-Up Tier 1 will expire no later than February 28, 2027, which the Exchange will indicate on the Exchange's Fee Schedule.
The proposed Step-Up Tier 1, like other Add Volume Tiers,
[
15
]
is intended to provide an additional opportunity to incentivize Members to earn an enhanced rebate by increasing their order flow to the Exchange, which further contributes to a deeper, more liquid market and provides even more execution opportunities for active market participants. Incentivizing an increase in liquidity adding volume through enhanced rebate opportunities encourages liquidity-adding Members on the Exchange to increase transactions and take execution opportunities provided by such increased liquidity, together providing for overall enhanced price discovery and price improvement opportunities on the Exchange. As such, increased overall order flow benefits all Members by contributing towards a
(
printed page 65274)
robust and well-balanced market ecosystem.
2. Statutory Basis
The Exchange believes the proposed rule change is consistent with the Act and the rules and regulations thereunder applicable to the Exchange and, in particular, the requirements of Section 6(b) of the Act.
5
Specifically, the Exchange believes the proposed rule change is consistent with the Section 6(b)(5)
6
requirements that the rules of an exchange be designed to prevent fraudulent and manipulative acts and practices, to promote just and equitable principles of trade, to foster cooperation and coordination with persons engaged in regulating, clearing, settling, processing information with respect to, and facilitating transactions in securities, to remove impediments to and perfect the mechanism of a free and open market and a national market system, and, in general, to protect investors and the public interest. Additionally, the Exchange believes the proposed rule change is consistent with the Section 6(b)(5)
7
requirement that the rules of an exchange not be designed to permit unfair discrimination between customers, issuers, brokers, or dealers as well as Section 6(b)(4)
8
as it is designed to provide for the equitable allocation of reasonable dues, fees and other charges among its Members and other persons using its facilities.
As described above, the Exchange operates in a highly competitive market in which market participants can readily direct order flow to competing venues if they deem fee levels at a particular venue to be excessive or incentives to be insufficient. The Exchange believes that its proposal to create Step-Up Tier 1 reflects a competitive pricing structure designed to incentivize market participants to direct their order flow to the Exchange, which the Exchange believes would enhance market quality to the benefit of all Members. Specifically, the Exchange's proposal to introduce Step-Up Tier 1 is not a significant departure from existing criteria, is reasonably correlated to the enhanced rebate offered by the Exchange and other competing exchanges,
[
16
]
and will continue to incentivize Members to submit order flow to the Exchange. Additionally, the Exchange notes that relative volume-based incentives and discounts have been widely adopted by exchanges,
[
17
]
including the Exchange,
[
18
]
and are reasonable, equitable and non-discriminatory because they are open to all Members on an equal basis and provide additional benefits or discounts that are reasonably related to (i) the value to an exchange's market quality and (ii) associated higher levels of market activity, such as higher levels of liquidity provision and/or growth patterns.
In particular, the Exchange believes its proposed Step-Up Tier 1 is reasonable because the proposed tier will be available to all Members and provides all Members with an opportunity to receive an enhanced rebate. The Exchange further believes its proposed Step-Up Tier 1 will provide a reasonable means to encourage liquidity adding displayed orders in Members' order flow to the Exchange and to incentivize Members to continue to provide liquidity adding volume to the Exchange as well as encourage Members to participate in CMC by offering them an opportunity to receive an enhanced rebate on qualifying orders. An overall increase in activity would deepen the Exchange's liquidity pool, offer additional cost savings, support the quality of price discovery, promote market transparency and improve market quality, for all investors.
The Exchange believes that its proposed Step-Up Tier 1 is reasonable as the proposed criteria does not represent a significant departure from the criteria currently offered in the Fee Schedule. The Exchange also believes that the proposal represents an equitable allocation of fees and rebates and is not unfairly discriminatory because all Members will be eligible for the proposed Step-Up Tier 1 and have the opportunity to meet the tier's criteria and receive the corresponding enhanced rebate if such criteria is met. While the Exchange has no way of predicting with certainty how the proposed changes will impact Member activity, based on the prior month's volume, the Exchange does not anticipate that any Member will be able to satisfy the proposed Step-Up Tier 1. The Exchange also notes that proposed changes will not adversely impact any Member's ability to qualify for enhanced rebates offered under other tiers. Should a Member not meet the proposed new criteria, the Member will merely not receive that corresponding enhanced rebate.
B. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement on Burden on Competition
The Exchange does not believe that the proposed rule change will impose any burden on competition that is not necessary or appropriate in furtherance of the purposes of the Act. Rather, as discussed above, the Exchange believes that the proposed change would encourage the submission of additional order flow to a public exchange, thereby promoting market depth, execution incentives and enhanced execution opportunities, as well as price discovery and transparency for all Members. As a result, the Exchange believes that the proposed changes further the Commission's goal in adopting Regulation NMS of fostering competition among orders, which promotes “more efficient pricing of individual stocks for all types of orders, large and small.”
The Exchange believes the proposed rule changes do not impose any burden on intramarket competition that is not necessary or appropriate in furtherance of the purposes of the Act. Particularly, the proposed creation of Step-Up Tier 1 does not impose an unnecessary burden as all Members are eligible to receive the enhanced rebate under the proposed tier. The Exchange does not believe the proposed changes burden competition, but rather, enhances competition as it is intended to increase the competitiveness of BZX by introducing a new pricing incentive in order to attract order flow and incentivize participants to increase their participation on the Exchange, providing for additional execution opportunities for market participants and improved price transparency. Greater overall order flow, trading opportunities, and pricing transparency benefits all market participants on the Exchange by enhancing market quality and continuing to encourage Members to send orders, thereby contributing towards a robust and well-balanced market ecosystem.
Next, the Exchange believes the proposed rule changes do not impose any burden on intermarket competition that is not necessary or appropriate in furtherance of the purposes of the Act. The Exchange operates in a highly competitive market. Members have numerous alternative venues that they may participate on and direct their order flow, including other equities exchanges, off-exchange venues, and alternative trading systems. Additionally, the Exchange represents a small percentage of the overall market. Based on publicly available information, no single equities exchange has more
(
printed page 65275)
than 14% of the market share.
[
19
]
Therefore, no exchange possesses significant pricing power in the execution of order flow. Indeed, participants can readily choose to send their orders to other exchange and off-exchange venues if they deem fee levels at those other venues to be more favorable. Moreover, the Commission has repeatedly expressed its preference for competition over regulatory intervention in determining prices, products, and services in the securities markets. Specifically, in Regulation NMS, the Commission highlighted the importance of market forces in determining prices and SRO revenues and, also, recognized that current regulation of the market system “has been remarkably successful in promoting market competition in its broader forms that are most important to investors and listed companies.”
[
20
]
The fact that this market is competitive has also long been recognized by the courts. In
NetCoalition
v.
Securities and Exchange Commission,
the D.C. Circuit stated as follows: “[n]o one disputes that competition for order flow is `fierce.' . . . As the SEC explained, `[i]n the U.S. national market system, buyers and sellers of securities, and the broker-dealers that act as their order-routing agents, have a wide range of choices of where to route orders for execution'; [and] `no exchange can afford to take its market share percentages for granted' because `no exchange possesses a monopoly, regulatory or otherwise, in the execution of order flow from broker dealers'. . . .”.
[
21
]
Accordingly, the Exchange does not believe its proposed fee change imposes any burden on competition that is not necessary or appropriate in furtherance of the purposes of the Act.
C. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement on Comments on the Proposed Rule Change Received From Members, Participants, or Others
The Exchange neither solicited nor received comments on the proposed rule change.
III. Date of Effectiveness of the Proposed Rule Change and Timing for Commission Action
The foregoing rule change has become effective pursuant to Section 19(b)(3)(A) of the Act
[
22
]
and paragraph (f) of Rule 19b-4
[
23
]
thereunder. At any time within 60 days of the filing of the proposed rule change, the Commission summarily may temporarily suspend such rule change if it appears to the Commission that such action is necessary or appropriate in the public interest, for the protection of investors, or otherwise in furtherance of the purposes of the Act. If the Commission takes such action, the Commission will institute proceedings to determine whether the proposed rule change should be approved or disapproved.
IV. Solicitation of Comments
Interested persons are invited to submit written data, views and arguments concerning the foregoing, including whether the proposed rule change is consistent with the Act. Comments may be submitted by any of the following methods:
Electronic Comments
Use the Commission's internet comment form (
https://www.sec.gov/​rules/​sro.shtml
); or
Send an email to
rule-comments@sec.gov
.
Please include file number
SR-CboeBZX-2026-084 on the subject line.
Paper Comments
Send paper comments in triplicate to Secretary, Securities and Exchange Commission, 100 F Street NE, Washington, DC 20549-1090.
All submissions should refer to file number SR-CboeBZX-2026-084. This file number should be included on the subject line if email is used. To help the Commission process and review your comments more efficiently, please use only one method. The Commission will post all comments on the Commission's internet website (
https://www.sec.gov/​rules/​sro.shtml
). Copies of the filing will be available for inspection and copying at the principal office of the Exchange. Do not include personal identifiable information in submissions; you should submit only information that you wish to make available publicly. We may redact in part or withhold entirely from publication submitted material that is obscene or subject to copyright protection. All submissions should refer to file number SR-CboeBZX-2026-084 and should be submitted on or before November 4, 2026.
For the Commission, by the Division of Trading and Markets, pursuant to delegated authority.
[
24
]
Sherry R. Haywood,
Assistant Secretary.

Securities and Exchange Commission
[Release No. 34-106639; File No. SR-TXSE-2026-035]
(
printed page 65283)
October 8, 2026.
Pursuant to Section 19(b)(1) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 (“Act”)
[
1
]
and Rule 19b-4 thereunder,
[
2
]
notice is hereby given that on October 1, 2026, Texas Stock Exchange LLC (“Exchange” or “TXSE”) filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission (“Commission”) the proposed rule change as described in Items I, II, and III below, which Items have been prepared by the Exchange. The Commission is publishing this notice to solicit comments on the proposed rule change from interested persons.
I. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement of the Terms of Substance of the Proposed Rule Change
The Exchange is filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission (“Commission”) a proposed rule change to amend the TXSE Fee Schedule to lower the transaction fee applicable to securities priced at or above $1.00 that remove displayed liquidity from the TXSE Book. The Exchange proposes to implement the rule change upon commencement of its operations as a national securities exchange.
The text of the proposed rule change is available on the Commission's website (
https://www.sec.gov/​rules/​sro.shtml
) at the Exchange's website (
https://www.txse.com/​regulations/​rules-filings
), and at the principal office of the Exchange.
II. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement of the Purpose of, and Statutory Basis for, the Proposed Rule Change
In its filing with the Commission, the Exchange included statements concerning the purpose of and basis for the proposed rule change and discussed any comments it received on the proposed rule change. The text of these statements may be examined at the places specified in Item IV below. The Exchange has prepared summaries, set forth in Sections A, B, and C below, of the most significant parts of such statements.
A. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement of the Purpose of, and Statutory Basis for, the Proposed Rule Change
1. Purpose
The Exchange proposes to amend Section A (Transaction Fees) of the TXSE Fee Schedule to reduce the fee for executions of orders that (i) are displayed on the TXSE Book and (ii) remove liquidity from the Exchange.
[
3
]
Currently, TXSE charges a fee of $0.0030 per share for these executions in securities priced at or above $1.00 per share. The Exchange now proposes to reduce this fee to $0.0029 per share and implement the change on October 1, 2026.
The proposed reduced fee for executions in securities priced at or above $1.00 per share that remove displayed liquidity is consistent with the fees charged by other exchanges for similar executions and the Exchange believes that reducing the fee for these transactions will encourage Members to increase the liquidity-removing orders they submit to the Exchange and result in increased interactions with displayed liquidity on the TXSE Book.
2. Statutory Basis
The Exchange believes the proposed rule change is consistent with the requirements of the Exchange Act. The Exchange believes that the proposed fee is consistent with the objectives of Section 6(b)(5) of the Act
[
4
]
in that they are designed to promote just and equitable principles of trade, to foster cooperation and coordination with persons engaged in regulating, clearing, settling, processing information with respect to, and facilitating transactions in securities, to remove impediments to and perfect the mechanism of a free and open market and national market system, and, in general, to protect investors and the public interest, and, particularly, are not designed to permit unfair discrimination between customers, issuers, brokers, or dealers. The Exchange also believes that the proposed rule change is consistent with the provisions of Section 6(b)(4) of the Act,
[
5
]
in that it is designed to provide for the equitable allocation of reasonable dues, fees, and other charges among its Members and other persons using its facilities.
The Exchange operates in a highly competitive market in which market participants can readily direct order flow to competing venues if they deem fee levels at a particular venue to be excessive or incentives to be insufficient. The Exchange believes that the proposed fee reflects a simple and competitive pricing change designed to incentivize market participants to direct their order flow to the Exchange, which the Exchange believes would promote price discovery and price formation and deepen liquidity that is subject to the Exchange's transparency, regulation, and oversight as an exchange, thereby enhancing market quality to the benefit of all Members and investors. The Commission and the courts have repeatedly expressed their preference for competition over regulatory intervention in determining prices, products, and services in the securities markets. In Regulation NMS, while adopting a series of steps to improve the current market model, the Commission highlighted the importance of market forces in determining prices and self-regulatory organization revenues, and also recognized that current regulation of the market system “has been remarkably successful in promoting market competition in its broader forms that are most important to investors and listed companies.
[
6
]
The Exchange believes that it is appropriate, reasonable, and consistent with the Act to reduce and now charge a standard fee of $0.0029 per share for executions of orders that remove liquidity from the TXSE Book in securities priced at or above $1.00 per share because it is comparable to the transaction fee charged by another exchange to remove liquidity.
[
7
]
The Exchange further believes that this fee is equitably allocated and not unfairly discriminatory because it applies equally to all Members and is designed to facilitate increased activity on the activity on the Exchange to the benefit of all Members by providing more trading opportunities and promoting price discovery.
(
printed page 65284)
B. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement on Burden on Competition
Section 6(b)(8) of the Act
[
8
]
requires that the Exchange's rules not impose any burden on competition that is not necessary or appropriate in furtherance of the purpose of the Exchange Act. The Exchange does not believe that the proposed rule change will result in any burden on competition that is not necessary or appropriate in furtherance of the purposes of the Act. Rather, as discussed above, the Exchange believes that the proposed fee change would encourage the submission of additional order flow to a public exchange, thereby promoting market depth, execution incentives, and enhanced execution opportunities, as well as price discovery and transparency for all Members. As a result, the Exchange believes that the proposed change furthers the Commission's goal in adopting Regulation NMS of fostering competition among orders, which promotes “more efficient pricing of individual stocks for all types of orders, large and small.”
[
9
]
The Exchange does not believe that the proposed rule change will impose any burden on intermarket competition that is not necessary or appropriate in furtherance of the purposes of the Act. To the contrary, the Exchange believes that the proposed fee change will increase competition and is intended to draw volume to the Exchange. The Exchange believes that the ever-shifting market share among the exchanges from month to month demonstrates that market participants can shift order flow or reduce use of certain categories of products in response to new or different pricing structures being introduced into the market. Accordingly, competitive forces constrain the Exchange's transaction fees, and market participants can readily trade on competing venues if they deem pricing levels at those other venues to be more favorable. Although this fee change is intended to attract liquidity to the Exchange, most other exchanges in operation today already offer multiple incentives to their participants, including tiered pricing that provides discounted executions, and other exchanges will be able to modify such incentives in order to compete with the Exchange. Accordingly, with respect to a participant deciding to submit an order to remove liquidity, there are multiple exchanges that will continue to be competitively priced for such orders when compared to the Exchange's pricing. Further, while pricing incentives can cause shifts of liquidity between trading centers, market participants make determinations on where to provide liquidity or route orders to take liquidity based on factors other than pricing, including execution quality, technology, functionality, and other considerations. Consequently, the Exchange believes that the degree to which its fees could impose any burden on competition is extremely limited and does not believe that such fees would burden competition of Members or competing venues in a manner that is not necessary or appropriate in furtherance of the purposes of the Act.
The Exchange does not believe that the proposed rule change will impose any burden on intramarket competition that is not necessary or appropriate in furtherance of the purposes of the Act because the proposed fee would apply equally to all Members. The proposed fee change is intended to encourage market participants to add liquidity to the Exchange by providing a competitive rate charged for removing liquidity, which the Exchange believes will help to encourage Members to send orders to the Exchange to the benefit of all Exchange participants. As the proposed rates are equally applicable to all market participants, the Exchange does not believe there is any burden on intramarket competition.
C. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement on Comments on the Proposed Rule Change Received From Members, Participants, or Others
The Exchange has neither solicited nor received written comments on the proposed rule change.
III. Date of Effectiveness of the Proposed Rule Change and Timing for Commission Action
The foregoing rule change has become effective pursuant to Section 19(b)(3)(A)(ii) of the Exchange Act
[
10
]
and Rule 19b-4(f)(2) thereunder,
[
11
]
because it establishes or changes a due, or fee.
At any time within 60 days of the filing of the proposed rule change, the Commission summarily may temporarily suspend the rule change if it appears to the Commission that the action is necessary or appropriate in the public interest, for the protection of investors, or would otherwise further the purposes of the Act. If the Commission takes such action, the Commission shall institute proceedings to determine whether the proposed rule should be approved or disapproved.
IV. Solicitation of Comments
Interested persons are invited to submit written data, views and arguments concerning the foregoing, including whether the proposed rule change is consistent with the Act. Comments may be submitted by any of the following methods:
Electronic Comments
Use the Commission's internet comment form (
https://www.sec.gov/​rules/​sro.shtml
); or
Send an email to
rule-comments@sec.gov
.
Please include file number SR-TXSE-2026-035 on the subject line.
Paper Comments
Send paper comments in triplicate to Secretary, Securities and Exchange Commission, 100 F Street NE, Washington, DC 20549-1090.
All submissions should refer to file number SR-TXSE-2026-035. This file number should be included on the subject line if email is used. To help the Commission process and review your comments more efficiently, please use only one method. The Commission will post all comments on the Commission's internet website (
https://www.sec.gov/​rules/​sro.shtml
). Copies of the filing will be available for inspection and copying at the principal office of the Exchange. Do not include personal identifiable information in submissions; you should submit only information that you wish to make available publicly. We may redact in part or withhold entirely from publication submitted material that is obscene or subject to copyright protection. All submissions should refer to file number SR-TXSE-2026-035 and should be submitted on or before November 4, 2026.
For the Commission, by the Division of Trading and Markets, pursuant to delegated authority.
[
12
]
Sherry R. Haywood,
Assistant Secretary.

Securities and Exchange Commission
[Release No. 34-106638; File No. SR-TXSE-2026-038]
October 8, 2026.
Pursuant to Section 19(b)(1) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 (“Act”),
[
1
]
and Rule 19b-4 thereunder,
[
2
]
notice is hereby given that on October 5, 2026, Texas Stock Exchange LLC (the “Exchange” or “TXSE”) filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission (“SEC” or “Commission”) the proposed rule change as described in Items I, II, and III below, which Items have been prepared by the Exchange. The Commission is publishing this notice to solicit comments on the proposed rule change from interested persons.
I. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement of the Terms of Substance of the Proposed Rule Change
The Exchange is filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission (“Commission”) a proposal to adopt the Shared Listings Program on the Exchange. The text of the proposed rule change is available on the Commission's website (
https://www.sec.gov/​rules/​sro.shtml
) at the Exchange's website (
https://www.txse.com/​regulations/​rules-filings
), and at the principal office of the Exchange.
II. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement of the Purpose of, and Statutory Basis for, the Proposed Rule Change
In its filing with the Commission, the Exchange included statements concerning the purpose of and basis for the proposed rule change and discussed any comments it received on the proposed rule change. The text of these statements may be examined at the places specified in Item IV below. The Exchange has prepared summaries, set forth in Sections A, B, and C below, of the most significant parts of such statements.
A. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement of the Purpose of, and Statutory Basis for, the Proposed Rule Change
1. Purpose
The Exchange proposes to add Section H to its Fee Schedule to establish a Shared Listings Program which provides certain credits that corporate issuers with the primary listing of a class of its stock (a “Primary Listing Company”) on the Exchange (excluding an Acquisition Company before consummation of its Business Combination as those terms are defined in Rule 16.313(a)(1)
[
3
]
) will receive related to the Exchange's revenue.
Background
The choice of listing exchange for public companies and companies looking to go public in the U.S. is effectively between two exchanges, operating as a duopoly in which listing decisions are based on the relative attractiveness of the two venues rather than a broad marketplace of alternatives. Their offerings are largely based on marketing and soft-dollar support that tends to obscure the true economic relationship between the exchanges and their listed companies. TXSE believes that issuers deserve a more transparent and economically rational framework for valuing a listing relationship. Accordingly, the Exchange proposes to implement a straightforward revenue-sharing structure under which eligible listed companies would receive a defined percentage of: the auction revenue generated by the Exchange in the issuer's security, the Exchange's proprietary market data revenue, and the annual listing fees they pay to the Exchange. This approach would allow issuers to evaluate the economic return of their listing decision in concrete, quantifiable terms, aligning the interests of the Exchange and its listed companies, promoting informed decision-making, and introducing meaningful price transparency to the competitive landscape.
Proposed Changes
The Exchange is proposing to adopt the Shared Listing Program, a fee arrangement that will provide transparent pricing and allocation of fees and credits to Primary Listing Companies. Specifically, the Exchange is proposing to issue an annual credit to Primary Listing Companies based on three factors: (i) the Exchange's auction transaction revenue attributable to the Primary Listing Company's securities (“Auction Credit”); (ii) the Exchange's Total Proprietary Market Data Revenue (“Market Data Credit”);
[
4
]
and (iii) the annual listing fee paid by the Primary Listing Company to the Exchange (“Listing Fee Credit” and, collectively
(
printed page 65277)
with the Auction Credit and Market Data Credit, “Total SLP Credit”).
Acquisition Companies would not be eligible to participate in the Shared Listings Program before consummation of their Business Combinations. Following consummation, a former Acquisition Company would become eligible prospectively, provided that it otherwise satisfies the requirements of the Program. Accordingly, the Exchange would calculate its credits solely by reference to trading days during which the issuer was eligible.
Auction Credit
Exchanges derive much of their listing revenue from opening and closing auctions in their primary listed securities. As such, the Exchange is proposing to allocate 30% of its annual auction transaction revenue from Opening and Closing Auctions in a Primary Listing Company's listed security or securities (“Total Auction Transaction Revenue”) in the form of an Auction Credit to the Primary Listing Company. This is calculated as Total Auction Transaction Revenue × .3. Total Auction Transaction Revenue will be calculated as the total transaction revenue for Opening and Closing Auctions during a given year. For example, where a Primary Listing Company has $100,000 in transaction revenue generated in the Opening and Closing Auctions in a given year in its listed corporate securities, the Exchange will provide the Primary Listing Company with a $30,000 Auction Credit ($100,000 × .3).
The Exchange believes that this marks a step forward in transparency around exchange economics and primary listings on the exchange. Exchanges derive much of their listings-related revenue from the Opening and Closing Auctions and listed companies do not currently receive any direct economic benefit from this lucrative portion of exchange listings. The value derived from Opening and Closing Auctions is easily measurable and listings with higher auction volume generate more revenue for their listing venue without meaningful incremental cost. As such, the Exchange is proposing to create a fee arrangement that is transparent to Primary Listing Companies and the marketplace by providing Primary Listing Companies with an Auction Credit that is based directly on how much revenue the Exchange derives from Opening and Closing Auctions in a particular security each year.
Market Data Credit
The Exchange is proposing to allocate 30% of its total proprietary market data revenue (the “Proprietary Market Data SLP Pool”) to a Market Data Credit to Primary Listing Companies, up to $100,000 per issuer. The calculation for allocation will be as follows:
Total Proprietary Market Data Revenue × .3 = Proprietary Market Data SLP Pool
Issuer Distribution Ratio = number of trading days Primary Listing Company had a primary listing on TXSE/total number of trading days that all Primary Listing Companies were listed on TXSE
Market Data Credit = the lesser of:
Proprietary Market Data SLP Pool * Issuer Distribution Ratio; and
$100,000
For example, Firm ABC was listed on the Exchange for 25% of the trading days in a year (63 trading days out of 252 total trading days), there were 9 other Primary Listing Companies for the entirety of the year (“Full Year Issuers”), and the Exchange had Total Proprietary Market Revenue of $3,333,333. The Proprietary Market Data SLP Pool is $3,333,333 × .3 = $1,000,000. The Issuer Distribution Ratio for Firm ABC is 63/((9 × 252) + 63) = .027027. Firm ABC would receive a Market Data Credit of the lesser of $27,027 (.027027 * $1,000,000) and $100,000, so Firm ABC would receive a Market Data Credit of $27,027. The Issuer Distribution Ratio for the Full Year Issuers would be 252/((9 × 252) + 63)) = .108108. The Full Year Issuers would receive a Market Data Credit of the lesser of $108,108 ($1,000,000 * .108108) and $100,000, so they would each receive a $100,000 Market Data Credit.
Again, the Exchange believes that sharing up to 30% of its Proprietary Market Data SLP Pool in the form of a Market Data Credit to Primary Listing Companies increases transparency between issuers and their listing venues and better reflects the economic reality for how exchanges are able to monetize their listing businesses. The more primary listings an exchange has on its market, the more valuable its proprietary market data becomes to market participants. Rather than obfuscating this from issuers, the Exchange is proposing to provide Primary Listing Companies with a Market Data Credit that allows them to share in the revenue the Exchange is generating from its proprietary market data products made more valuable by their listing.
Listing Fee Credit
The Exchange is also proposing to allocate 30% of a Primary Listing Company's annual listing fees from the prior year back to each Primary Listing Company in the form of a Listing Fee Credit (
e.g.,
30% of a $100,000 annual listing fee paid in 2026 would be a $30,000 Listing Fee Credit in 2027). This is intended to further share the economics of listings with Primary Listing Companies on the Exchange and to act as a further incentive for Primary Listing Companies to remain listed with the Exchange. As an example, where a Primary Listing Company paid $100,000 in annual listing fees to the Exchange (which excludes any initial fees, application fees, corporate action fees, etc.) for the prior year, in the following year the Exchange would issue a $30,000 Listing Fee Credit to the Primary Listing Company. Consistent with the Auction Credit and the Market Data Credit, the Listing Fee Credit will more directly tie the economics of listing on the Exchange to the revenue that the listing generates for the Exchange.
Total SLP Credit
In January of each year, the Exchange will calculate each Primary Listing Company's Market Data Credit, Auction Credit, and Listing Fee Credit for the previous year and add them together to calculate the Total SLP Credit. A Primary Listing Company's Total SLP Credit can then be applied to any fees incurred by the Primary Listing Company related to the listing of their corporate security or securities on the Exchange for that upcoming year, as the Exchange bills its annual listing fees in January of each year. A Primary Listing Company may opt to have the Total SLP Credit applied to then applicable corporate listing fees on the Exchange or opt to receive payment from the Exchange of all or part of their Total SLP Credit.
[
5
]
The Total SLP Credit
(
printed page 65278)
expires at the close of business on the last trading day of January and cannot be carried over or transferred to another party.
2. Statutory Basis
The Exchange believes that the proposed rule change is consistent with Section 6(b) of the Act,
[
6
]
in general, and furthers the objectives of Sections 6(b)(4) and (5) of the Act,
[
7
]
in particular, in that it provides for the equitable allocation of reasonable dues, fees and other charges among issuers and it does not unfairly discriminate between customers, issuers, brokers or dealers.
The Exchange believes that the proposed adoption of the Shared Listings Program is a reasonable, fair and equitable, and not unfairly discriminatory allocation of fees and other charges because it would create a distribution of fees and other charges applicable to all issuers that reflect the additional revenue that a listing on the Exchange creates for the Exchange through executions occurring in the auctions, market data revenue, and listing fees. The Shared Listings Program acknowledges the additional revenue brought to the TXSE by its listed securities and is designed to reward an issuer for such additional revenue, which TXSE believes will create a more equitable appropriate relationship between the TXSE and Primary Listing Companies based on the revenue and expenses associated with listing on TXSE. As such, the Exchange believes that it is reasonable, fair and equitable, and not unfairly discriminatory allocation of fees and other charges to provide credits to Primary Listing Companies listed on the Exchange.
[
8
]
The Exchange believes that it is reasonable, fair and equitable, and not unfairly discriminatory to apply the Shared Listings Program to corporate listings and not to ETP listings because the economics of corporate listings and ETP listings are similar but different and the Exchange has a fee arrangement for ETPs that is more specifically tailored to ETPs.
The Exchange believes that excluding Acquisition Companies before consummation of their Business Combinations is reasonable, equitable, and not unfairly discriminatory. Acquisition Companies differ from operating companies because, as provided in TXSE Rule 16.313(a)(1), they have no prior operating history and hold at least 90% of their offering proceeds and concurrent equity-sale proceeds in trust pending a Business Combination. The Shared Listings Program is intended to share the economics associated with an ongoing primary-listing relationship with an operating company. Before consummating a Business Combination, an Acquisition Company is a shell company without an operating business and is listed under a distinct regulatory framework reflecting its limited purpose of identifying and completing a Business Combination. It therefore is not similarly situated to the operating companies for which the Shared Listings Program is designed. An Acquisition Company that consummates its Business Combination would become eligible to participate in the Shared Listings Program at that time. Following consummation of its Business Combination, the company becomes an operating company and is similarly situated to other eligible operating companies participating in the Program. The proposed exclusion therefore distinguishes between issuers based on objective differences in their status and applies uniformly to all similarly situated issuers.
The Exchange believes that providing an Auction Credit to a Primary Listing Company based on the specific auction transaction volume of its listed securities is a reasonable, fair and equitable, and not unfairly discriminatory allocation of fees and other charges because it would create a distribution of fees and other charges applicable to all eligible issuers that are commensurate with the additional revenue that a security listed on the Exchange creates for the Exchange through executions occurring in the Opening and Closing Auctions. As described above, where the auction volume of a security increases, so does the additional auction transaction fee revenue earned by the primary listing exchange. Accordingly, awarding an Auction Credit on the basis of the total transaction revenue from Opening and Closing Auctions on the Exchange will reward the Primary Listing Company on the basis of the additional revenue that the security brought to the Exchange during the prior year. Further to this point, the Exchange does not believe that the proposal is unfairly discriminatory because, as described above, the annual Auction Credit is based on the additional revenue that the Exchange has received from the security being listed on the Exchange. The Exchange also believes that it is equitable and not unfairly discriminatory for securities with high auction volume to receive a larger Auction Credit than securities with lower auction volume because the Auction Credit is directly proportionate to the amount of revenue generated for the Exchange through the Opening and Closing Auctions.
Similarly, the Exchange believes that providing the same Market Data Credit to all Primary Listing Companies capped at $100,000 per year is a reasonable, fair and equitable, and not unfairly discriminatory allocation of fees and other charges because it would create a distribution of fees and other charges applicable to all Primary Listing Companies that represents a percentage of the revenue that they collectively bring to the Exchange in the form of more useful market data. There is no reliably accurate way to calculate the specific contribution of particular securities to proprietary market revenue and, as noted above, the more listed securities there are on a particular exchange the more useful that exchange's market data becomes, so the Exchange believes that providing proportionally equal payments to all Primary Listing Companies based on the amount of time they're listed on the Exchange is a reasonable allocation of fees and other charges. The Exchange believes that capping the Market Data Credit at $100,000 is consistent with the Act because it provides a cap that the Exchange believes to be reasonable while still providing a substantial Market Data Credit to each Primary Listing Company.
The Exchange believes that providing a Listing Fee Credit to all Primary Listing Companies of 30% of their annual listing fee is a reasonable, fair and equitable, and not unfairly discriminatory allocation of fees and other charges because it would create a distribution of fees and other charges applicable to all Primary Listing Companies directly tied to the Exchange's revenue from their annual listing fee. Consistent with the Auction Credit and the Market Data Credit, the Listing Fee Credit will more directly tie the economics of listing on the Exchange to the revenue that the listing generates for the Exchange.
The Exchange believes that the application of the Total SLP Credit is a
(
printed page 65279)
reasonable, fair and equitable, and not unfairly discriminatory allocation of fees and other charges because, as noted throughout this proposal, the Shared Listings Program represents a more transparent and equitable allocation of fees for corporate listings based on revenue generated by the Exchange. More specifically, the Exchange believes that the ability for a Primary Listing Company to apply the Total SLP Credit to its applicable corporate listing fees or to receive payment for such credit is a reasonable, fair and equitable, and not unfairly discriminatory allocation of fees and other charges because it reflects the economics of the listing relationship with the Exchange and provides additional flexibility to Primary Listing Companies by allowing them to opt to receive the same economic benefit in multiple ways. The Exchange also notes that other exchange listing programs related to ETPs have allowed for payments to issuers based on the economics to the listing exchange.
[
9
]
While this proposal relates specifically to corporate listings and not ETPs, the Exchange believes that the underlying policy rationale for allowing the payments is the same—exchanges benefit from the economics of a listing (whether ETP or corporate listing) beyond just the annual listing fees and the fee arrangements should reflect those benefits which would include payment to issuers based on these economics.
B. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement on Burden on Competition
The Exchange does not believe that the proposed rule change will impose any burden on competition that is not necessary or appropriate in furtherance of the purposes of the Exchange Act. The Exchange believes that the proposed rule change will improve competition by enhancing competition as it is intended to increase the competitiveness of the Exchange's listings program by allowing the Exchange to provide Primary Listing Companies with listing credit and/or payments based on the revenue generated by the Exchange.
The Exchange believes that the proposed rule change would increase both intermarket and intramarket competition by increasing the competitiveness of its listing venue and attracting eligible transfer and new listings on the Exchange.
The exclusion of Acquisition Companies before consummation of their Business Combinations would not impose an unnecessary or inappropriate burden on competition because it would apply uniformly to all Acquisition Companies. Following consummation of a Business Combination, the resulting operating company would be eligible to participate prospectively on the same terms as other eligible Primary Listing Companies.
C. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement on Comments on the Proposed Rule Change Received From Members, Participants or Others
The Exchange neither solicited nor received written comments on the proposed rule change.
III. Date of Effectiveness of the Proposed Rule Change and Timing for Commission Action
The foregoing rule change has become effective pursuant to Section 19(b)(3)(A) of the Act
[
10
]
and Rule 19b-4(f)(2)
[
11
]
thereunder. At any time within 60 days of the filing of the proposed rule change, the Commission summarily may temporarily suspend such rule change if it appears to the Commission that such action is necessary or appropriate in the public interest, for the protection of investors, or otherwise in furtherance of the purposes of the Act. If the Commission takes such action, the Commission will institute proceedings to determine whether the proposed rule change should be approved or disapproved.
IV. Solicitation of Comments
Interested persons are invited to submit written data, views and arguments concerning the foregoing, including whether the proposed rule change is consistent with the Act. Comments may be submitted by any of the following methods:
Electronic Comments
Use the Commission's internet comment form (
https://www.sec.gov/​rules/​sro.shtml
); or
Send an email to
rule-comments@sec.gov
.
Please include file number SR-TXSE-2026-038 on the subject line.
Paper Comments
Send paper comments in triplicate to Secretary, Securities and Exchange Commission, 100 F Street NE, Washington, DC 20549-1090.
All submissions should refer to file number SR-TXSE-2026-038. This file number should be included on the subject line if email is used. To help the Commission process and review your comments more efficiently, please use only one method. The Commission will post all comments on the Commission's internet website (
https://www.sec.gov/​rules/​sro.shtml
). Copies of the filing will be available for inspection and copying at the principal office of the Exchange. Do not include personal identifiable information in submissions; you should submit only information that you wish to make available publicly. We may redact in part or withhold entirely from publication submitted material that is obscene or subject to copyright protection. All submissions should refer to file number SR-TXSE-2026-038 and should be submitted on or before November 4, 2026.
For the Commission, by the Division of Trading and Markets, pursuant to delegated authority.
[
12
]
Sherry R. Haywood,
Assistant Secretary.

October 8, 2026.
Pursuant to Section 19(b)(1) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 (the “Act”),
[
1

and Rule 19b-4 thereunder,
[
2
]
notice is hereby given that on October 7, 2026, Texas Stock Exchange LLC (the “Exchange” or “TXSE”) filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission (“Commission”) a proposed rule change as described in Items I, II, and III below, which Items have been prepared by the Exchange. The Commission is publishing this notice to solicit comments on the proposed rule change from interested persons.
I. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement of the Terms of Substance of the Proposed Rule Change
The Exchange is filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission (“Commission”) a proposal to adopt Rodeo II on the Exchange. The text of the proposed rule change is available on the Commission's website (
https://www.sec.gov/​rules/​sro.shtml
) at the Exchange's website (
https://
(
printed page 65280)
www.txse.com/​regulations/​rules-filings
), and at the principal office of the Exchange.
II. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement of the Purpose of, and Statutory Basis for, the Proposed Rule Change
In its filing with the Commission, the Exchange included statements concerning the purpose of and basis for the proposed rule change and discussed any comments it received on the proposed rule change. The text of these statements may be examined at the places specified in Item IV below. The Exchange has prepared summaries, set forth in Sections A, B, and C below, of the most significant parts of such statements.
A. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement of the Purpose of, and Statutory Basis for, the Proposed Rule Change
1. Purpose
The Exchange proposes to implement Rodeo II to provide the first ten issuers of corporate securities that on or before December 31, 2026 either transfer their primary listing to TXSE or dually list on TXSE (the “Founding Partners”), subject to certain requirements below, with restricted stock units of the Exchange's parent holding company, TXSE Group Inc. (“TXSE Group”), that will vest over the course of two years.
[
3
]
Qualifying listings completed beginning on October 5, including those completed before the commencement of the Program, are eligible to participate.
[
4
]
Rodeo II will commence on October 7, 2026 and run until the earliest of: (i) the allocation of all available awards; (ii) December 31, 2026; or (iii) the Exchange, in its sole discretion, terminates the Program. If there are more than ten Founding Partners on or before December 31, 2026, TXSE may, in its sole discretion, increase the total number of restricted share awards to 15 upon providing notice on its website. Any such increase would be subject to the same requirements applicable to the first 10 awards. Founding Partners may be, but are not required to be, current investors in TXSE Group, and the Exchange anticipates both current investors and new participants participating in the Program. The total equity ownership of TXSE Group Stock shall be subject to the ownership limitations of the Eighth Amended and Restated Stockholders' Agreement of TXSE Group Inc. as amended (the “TXSE Group Stockholders' Agreement”) and of the Certificate of Formation of TXSE Group Inc. (the “TXSE Group Certificate of Formation”).
[
5
]
The purpose of Rodeo II is to promote the long-term interests of the Exchange by providing incentives designed to recognize the contribution of qualifying issuers that transferred their listings to TXSE at the launch of its corporate listing business, attract additional qualifying primary and dual listings, and encourage all Founding Partners to retain their listings on TXSE for at least two years, as further described below. Founding Partners' equity interest in TXSE Group will also help to align long-term incentives among corporate issuers more broadly, the Exchange, and its parent company by adding more corporate issuers to TXSE Group's ownership group and more specifically for the Founding Partners by providing issuers with the opportunity to share in the benefits of TXSE's increased enterprise value.
To be eligible to be a Founding Partner, a company must: (i) be a United States domiciled issuer whose primary listing consist solely of either: (a) common stock issued by a corporation (including an operating company or a business development company regulated under the Investment Company Act of 1940); (b) master limited partnership units; or (c) common shares of a real estate investment trust (“REIT”);
[
6
]
(ii) satisfy, or have satisfied at the time of listing, the Exchange's quantitative listing standards applicable to the transfer of a primary listing or addition of a dual listing of such securities to TXSE, and receive, or have received, approval to list from TXSE Regulation; (iii) (a) for primary listings, have a trailing 90-trading day average market capitalization of at least $3.5 billion at the time of the primary listing transfer or at the end of the first trading day that the applicant is primarily listed on TXSE; or (b) for dual listings, have a market cap of at least $100 billion; (iv) execute all required Program documentation, including a subscription agreement, listing application, and confidentiality agreement; (v) complete or have completed the transfer of a primary listing or a dual listing, as applicable, of a qualifying class of equity securities to the Exchange which shall be deemed completed upon the first Opening Auction in the equity security on the Exchange.
Where an issuer satisfies the above conditions, they will receive 100,000 restricted stock units (the “Rodeo Units”) within sixty days following completion of the listing. Rodeo Units will vest in two tranches subject to the maintenance of the applicable continued listing standards on the Exchange as follows:
For primary listings:
Fifty percent of the Rodeo Units will vest upon the first anniversary of the issuer's continuous primary listing on the Texas Stock Exchange, provided that the issuer remains primarily listed on the Exchange as of such date; and
Fifty percent of the Rodeo Units will vest on the second anniversary of the issuer's continuous primary listing on the Texas Stock Exchange, provided that the issuer remains primarily listed on the Exchange as of such date.
For dual listings:
Fifty percent of the Rodeo Units will vest upon the first anniversary of the issuer's continuous listing (whether a dual listing or a primary listing) on the Texas Stock Exchange, provided that the issuer remains listed on the Exchange as of such date; and
Fifty percent of the Rodeo Units will vest on the second anniversary of the issuer's continuous listing (whether a dual listing or a primary listing) on the Texas Stock Exchange, provided that the issuer remains listed on the Exchange as of such date.
(
printed page 65281)
2. Statutory Basis
The Exchange believes that the proposed rule change is consistent with Section 6(b) of the Act,
[
7
]
in general, and furthers the objectives of Section 6(b)(5) of the Act,
[
8
]
in particular, in that it is designed to prevent fraudulent and manipulative acts and practices, to promote just and equitable principles of trade, to foster cooperation and coordination with persons engaged in facilitating transactions in securities, to remove impediments to and perfect the mechanisms of a free and open market and a national market system and, in general, to protect investors and the public interest. Additionally, the Exchange believes the proposed rule change is consistent with the requirement in Section 6(b)(5) of the Act
[
9
]
that the rules of an exchange not be designed to permit unfair discrimination between customers, issuers, brokers, or dealers. The Exchange also believes the proposed rule change is consistent with Section 6(b)(4) of the Act,
[
10
]
which requires that Exchange rules provide for the equitable allocation of reasonable dues, fees, and other charges among its members and other persons using its facilities.
TXSE notes that the Exchange operates in a highly competitive marketplace for the listing of companies.
[
11
]
The Commission has repeatedly expressed its preference for competition over regulatory intervention in determining prices, products, and services in the securities markets. The Exchange believes that the ever-shifting market share among exchanges with respect to new listings and the transfer of existing listings between competitor exchanges demonstrates that issuers can choose different listing markets in response to fee changes and this proposal is designed to help the Exchange both compete for new listings and retain existing listings. Moreover, new competitors, such as the Exchange, can enter the space, as well as existing exchanges currently without listing programs and new fee arrangements, such as Rodeo II, act to further enhance new entrants' ability to compete in the listings business. Accordingly, competitive forces constrain the Exchange's listing fees and incentive programs like Rodeo II can have a direct effect on the ability of TXSE to compete for new listings and retain existing listings.
The Exchange believes that the proposal is equitable and not unfairly discriminatory because participation is available on the same terms to qualifying issuers that have already transferred their listings to TXSE and to qualifying issuers that subsequently transfer their primary listings or dually list on the Exchange, subject to the Program's eligibility criteria and award limits. Including the five issuers that transferred their listings at the launch of the Exchange's corporate listing business recognizes their contribution to establishing TXSE as a corporate listing venue and provides an incentive for them to maintain their listings through the applicable vesting dates. Providing the same award and applying the same listing-based vesting conditions to existing and subsequent qualifying participants supports the Program's objectives of attracting and retaining an initial group of corporate issuers and aligning their long-term interests with the growth of the Exchange. The eligibility criteria are objective and apply equally to existing and subsequent qualifying participants. The eligibility criteria are equitable and not unfairly discriminatory in that the Exchange is trying to attract companies of a particular type (U.S. domiciled corporations, MLPs, and REITs) and size (greater than $3.5 billion market cap for primary listing and $100 billion for dual listing) to list on the Exchange in order to help establish its corporate listing business. The Exchange believes that these are reasonable and not unfairly discriminatory because they represent the types of companies that the Exchange wants to attract and retain and it wants to provide additional incentives for such companies to list and remain listed on the Exchange. The Exchange has focused the Program on these types of companies because it believes attracting and retaining an initial group of these issuers will help establish TXSE as a competitive corporate listing venue and encourage additional issuers to list on the Exchange. As noted above, the competition for listings is robust and the Exchange believes that Rodeo II will enhance competition between the exchanges for listings.
Further to this point, an equity interest in TXSE Group is intended to align participating issuers' long-term interests with the development of the Exchange's listing business. The Exchange intends to develop separate incentive programs for other security types, tailored to their respective characteristics and the Exchange's objectives in attracting those listings. The Exchange believes that attracting companies that meet these criteria will bring greater future value to TXSE as a listing venue than companies that do not meet these criteria.
The Exchange believes that having higher standards for participation for dual-listings is reasonable and not unfairly discriminatory because the Exchange wants to incentivize primary listings on TXSE. The Exchange prioritizes primary listings because they establish TXSE as an issuer's principal listing venue and provide the foundation for a durable corporate listing franchise. Attracting primary listings across a broader range of eligible issuers can help demonstrate the Exchange's capabilities and encourage subsequent listings. The Exchange therefore believes broader eligibility for primary listings is consistent with the Program's objective of developing its corporate listing business.
For dual listings, the Exchange has established a higher market capitalization threshold because the issuer retains its primary listing on another exchange. The Exchange believes that attracting issuers with a market capitalization of at least $100 billion can provide particular visibility and recognition for TXSE among other prospective issuers. The threshold is intended to focus the Program's equity incentives on dual listings that the Exchange believes can make a substantial contribution to establishing its corporate listing franchise.
The Exchange also believes that Founding Partners' equity interest in TXSE Group will help to align long-term incentives among corporate issuers more broadly, the Exchange, and its parent company by adding more corporate issuers to TXSE Group's ownership group and more specifically for the Founding Partners by providing issuers with the opportunity to share in the benefits of TXSE's increased enterprise value.
The Exchange believes that the vesting period is equitable and reasonable because it ensures that only issuers that transfer to the Exchange and remain listed on the Exchange for at least one year will partially vest and for two years will fully vest. The Exchange believes that requiring Founding Partners to remain listed for a period of two years in order to fully vest will further help establish the Exchange as a
(
printed page 65282)
listing venue.
[
12
]
As noted above, Founding Partners may be, but are not required to be, current investors in TXSE Group, and the Exchange anticipates both current and potential new investors to participate in the Program. The total equity ownership of TXSE Group Stock shall be subject to the ownership limitations of the TXSE Group Stockholders' Agreement and the TXSE Group Certificate of Formation.
[
13
]
The Exchange believes the Rodeo II Program is equitable and reasonable because attracting and retaining listings from the type and size of companies that the Program is intended to attract will, in addition to benefitting the Exchange's listing business, also help to attract and retain additional liquidity and transaction volume on the Exchange. Such additional liquidity will benefit all market participants by providing tighter quoting and better prices on the Exchange, all of which works to perfect the mechanism for a free and open market and national market system.
B. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement on Burden on Competition
The Exchange does not believe that the proposed rule change will impose any burden on
competition that is not necessary or appropriate in furtherance of the purposes of the Exchange Act. The Exchange believes that the proposed rule change will improve competition by aligning long-term incentives among corporate issuers with the Exchange's parent company and providing qualifying existing issuers with an incentive to remain listed on the Exchange and additional qualifying issuers with an incentive to list and remain listed on the Exchange.
The Exchange believes that the proposed rule change would increase both intermarket and intramarket competition by encouraging qualifying issuers already listed on TXSE to maintain their listings and encouraging additional qualifying issuers to transfer their primary listings or dually list on the Exchange. The five issuers that transferred their listings at the launch of the Exchange's corporate listing business have contributed to establishing TXSE as a listing venue. Their continued listing, together with additional qualifying listings, would help develop the Exchange's corporate listing business and encourage other issuers to consider TXSE as their listing venue. To the extent that there is an additional competitive burden on non-Founding Partners, the Exchange believes that this is appropriate because the development of an additional competitive listing venue would benefit all issuers.
Although five issuers have already transferred their listings to TXSE, retaining those issuers and attracting additional qualifying issuers remain important to developing a durable corporate listing business. Rodeo II is limited to an initial group of ten qualifying issuers, subject to the potential increase to fifteen described above. The Exchange believes that a program of this limited scope would enhance its ability to compete for and retain listings without imposing an inappropriate burden on competition. Additional primary listing transfers would increase TXSE's listings and reduce listings on competing venues, while retention of existing listings and additional dual listings would support the development of TXSE's listing business. The Program would also provide qualifying issuers with an additional factor to consider when choosing whether to list or remain listed on TXSE.
C. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement on Comments on the Proposed Rule Change Received From Members, Participants or Others
The Exchange neither solicited nor received written comments on the proposed rule change.
III. Date of Effectiveness of the Proposed Rule Change and Timing for Commission Action
The foregoing rule change has become effective pursuant to Section 19(b)(3)(A) of the Act
[
14
]
and Rule 19b-4(f)(2)
[
15
]
thereunder. At any time within 60 days of the filing of the proposed rule change, the Commission summarily may temporarily suspend such rule change if it appears to the Commission that such action is necessary or appropriate in the public interest, for the protection of investors, or otherwise in furtherance of the purposes of the Act. If the Commission takes such action, the Commission will institute proceedings to determine whether the proposed rule change should be approved or disapproved.
IV. Solicitation of Comments
Interested persons are invited to submit written data, views and arguments concerning the foregoing, including whether the proposal is consistent with the Act. Comments may be submitted by any of the following methods:
Electronic Comments
Use the Commission's internet comment form (
https://www.sec.gov/​rules/​sro.shtml
); or
Send an email to
rule-comments@sec.gov
.
Please include File No. SR-TXSE-2026-039 on the subject line.
Paper Comments
Send paper comments in triplicate to Secretary, Securities and Exchange Commission, 100 F Street NE, Washington, DC 20549-1090.
All submissions should refer to File No. SR-TXSE-2026-039. This file number should be included on the subject line if email is used. To help the Commission process and review your comments more efficiently, please use only one method. The Commission will post all comments on the Commission's internet website (
https://www.sec.gov/​rules/​sro.shtml
). Copies of the filing will be available for inspection and copying at the principal office of the Exchange. Do not include personal identifiable information in submissions; you should submit only information that you wish to make available publicly. We may redact in part or withhold entirely from publication submitted material that is obscene or subject to copyright protection. All submissions should refer to file number SR-TXSE-2026-039 and should be submitted on or before November 4, 2026.

]
